name: Hashimoto Thyroiditis

ethnicAssociations: All ethnicities; most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ATA/ETA Clinical Guidelines for Hashimoto Thyroiditis

criteria.description: Thyroid ultrasound showing diffuse hypoechogenicity and heterogeneity
FNA or histology showing lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers and Hurthle cell change

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hypothyroidism (elevated TSH) plus positive anti-TPO or anti-thyroglobulin antibodies. Ultrasound findings supportive but not required.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Can present initially with transient thyrotoxicosis (hashitoxicosis) before progressing to hypothyroidism. Euthyroid Hashimoto's (positive antibodies with normal thyroid function) exists and may progress.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-tender diffuse goiter with firm rubbery texture
pathognomonic.notes: Gradually developing; may eventually atrophy in late disease

rare.notes: Steroid-responsive encephalopathy associated with autoimmune thyroiditis; seizures, myoclonus, cognitive decline
Life-threatening; hypothermia, altered consciousness, cardiovascular collapse
Rapidly enlarging goiter; increased risk compared to general population

laboratory: Low free T4 (overt hypothyroidism) or normal free T4 (subclinical hypothyroidism)
Macrocytic anemia (associated vitamin B12 deficiency/pernicious anemia)
imaging: Thyroid ultrasound: diffuse hypoechogenicity, heterogeneous echotexture, micronodularity, increased vascularity (early), decreased vascularity (late/atrophic)
Thyroid uptake scan: decreased uptake (in hypothyroid phase); heterogeneous uptake
other: FNA cytology: lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal centers, Hurthle (oncocytic) cell change, atrophic follicles
Histology: dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, follicular destruction, fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse increased uptake on thyroid scan

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging thyroid nodule (concern for thyroid lymphoma or carcinoma)
Severe hypothyroidism with altered consciousness (myxedema coma)
Compressive symptoms (dysphagia, stridor) from large goiter
Signs of associated autoimmune conditions (type 1 diabetes, Addison disease)
references: Garber JR, et al. Clinical practice guidelines for hypothyroidism in adults: cosponsored by the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists and the American Thyroid Association. Thyroid. 2012;22(12):1200-1235.
Pearce EN, et al. Clinical practice. Hashimoto's thyroiditis. N Engl J Med. 2003;348(26):2646-2655.
Caturegli P, et al. Hashimoto thyroiditis: clinical and diagnostic criteria. Autoimmun Rev. 2014;13(4-5):391-397.
